item.title: ‘You Call Him Out’ — Former Steelers Star Unimpressed With Mike McCarthy’s Handling of DK Metcalf’s Ejection
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf faced a difficult situation as he was ejected in the third quarter of the Steelers’ game against the Philadelphia Eagles, which ended in a 19-16 loss. The wide receiver was seen losing his composure as he appeared to get physical with safety Cooper DeJean. Metcalf was ejected shortly after he was seen poking DeJean in the eye. Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy seen on the sideline during the first quarter of an NFL game against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Steelers Legend Criticizes McCarthy over Metcalf Ejection In a recent episode of ‘NFL on CBS’, two-time Super Bowl champion with the Steelers Bryant McFadden shared his views on the wide receiver’s ejection and how the coaching staff handled it. He said: “I didn’t like how he (McCarthy) handled it. I think we’re in a moment now where we’re starting to see this become a recurring theme for DK. You brought up something that I totally forgot about a year ago, against Detroit, when he got into a spat with a fan in the stands while the game was going on.” “I didn’t like how [Mike McCarthy] handled it.” @BMac_SportsTalk talks about DK Metcalf’s ejection and how the coaching staff dealt with it. #Scoreboard pic.twitter.com/bZJoqputNm — NFL on CBS (@NFLonCBS) November 22, 2026 Metcalf’s ejection came in the third quarter. He was initially flagged for taunting and was subsequently ejected for unsportsmanlike conduct. When asked about the ejection, head coach Mike McCarthy said: “We need him (Metcalf). We need him in those games, and that’s not acceptable to get thrown out of the game,” and added, “We can’t have players getting ejected from games.” McFadden shared his point of view on the head coach’s reaction and said: “Now, Mike McCarthy was not the head coach. That was Mike T. But clearly, Mike McCarthy … you’re aware of some of these past actions by DK. At that time, that’s when you call him out in a respectful, professional way. We cannot tolerate this. These are non-negotiables.” The ejection wasn’t the only thing Metcalf caught flak for after week 11’s game as he has also been facing criticism for leaving the stadium before the reporters were let in. When asked about it on Monday, Metcalf admitted he was avoiding the media, adding to fans’ frustration. The head coach’s comments caught McFadden’s attention, as he believed that McCarthy was saying things that everyone already knew. Fans and analysts would like to know what the head coach would have told the wide receiver in a professional manner. It will be interesting to see how the head coach deals with this recurring situation involving the wide receiver, as this is Metcalf’s third ejection since entering the NFL in 2019, tying Dre Greenlaw for the most disqualifications over that span. item.title: Quiet around potential Simon Holmstrom extension talks could prove best for Islanders star after key change
item.description: Simon Holmstrom (92) of the New York Islanders reacts after scoring a goal against the Anaheim Ducks in Anaheim, Calif., Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026. Things have stayed quiet around a potential contract extension for Simon Holmstrom, and right now, it certainly behooves the Islanders’ winger to keep waiting rather than negotiate in-season. Not only because of the salary cap boom that keeps lifting contracts higher and higher, but also because Holmstrom’s play so far this season is reshaping his value entirely. Holmstrom has always had the potential to score a lot more than he did and to play a lot higher up in the lineup than he had. He’s finally realizing it now. Coming into Monday night’s game against the Maple Leafs, he was riding a hot streak of six goals and 11 points in his past seven games. He has been on the Islanders’ top line for over a month, and the lack of confidence he would sometimes display in that spot in years past is completely gone. “When I think back, obviously I had a lot of chances to watch last year [while out with a torn ACL]. I think this year, you see him being more in an attack mindset, even when he’s going to work,” Kyle Palmieri, who’s played alongside Holmstrom and Bo Horvat for most of this season, told The Post. “I noticed it last game [in Detroit], especially below the goal line. He’s doing it in an attack mode as opposed to, ‘Where do I pass this to?’ Simon Holmstrom (92) of the New York Islanders reacts after scoring a goal against the Anaheim Ducks in Anaheim, Calif., Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026. NHLI via Getty Images “He’s looking to get a step on a guy or use his long reach to carry up to the net or find a guy in the slot that’s open. I think when you look at his goal the other night, he’s putting himself in scoring areas and obviously finishing too.” The numbers and charts back up Palmieri’s eyes. Holmstrom is shooting between the dots at an exceptional rate, and all of his goals have come from there as well. He’s averaging an extra 1.21 shots and 2.07 attempts per 60 minutes this season compared to last, both career highs, and it hasn’t yet hurt his shooting percentage. Over 25 percent of the way through the season, Holmstrom is on a 38-goal, 68-point pace. A year ago, a suggestion that Holmstrom’s next contract would be worth $8 million annually would have been laughed out of the room. In this cap environment and with that production, $8 million may constitute a bargain, should Holmstrom keep this up. “That’s up to my agents and [Islanders general manager Mathieu Darche] and those guys,” Holmstrom told The Post when asked whether negotiations have picked up. “I don’t think about that at all. He played parts of four seasons at East Carolina before spending the 2024 season in Raleigh, where he had a career year: .378/.438/.753 with 24 homers and a 168 wRC+. He also had 5 defensive runs saved, and thus ended with a 5.4 WAR — the 14th-best among all Division I players in 2024. As a minor leaguer, Briley shows promise but still has yet to stand out among the crowd. Although he’s earned SSS’s Minor League Player of Week and Month accolades, his development at the plate hadn’t hit a stride deemed major league-worthy yet. Until 2026. Briley unlocked power in his swing, joining the 30-home run club while clubbing a .490 slugging percentage in Double-A. Although he still hasn’t duplicated the all-around plate success he exhibited in his rookie year in Single-A, Briley kicked his hitting up a notch. His added patience at the plate and extra bags swiped nod to a potentially evolved level of maturity. Double-A is often a big test for young players, and Briley met the challenge. Although Briley might’ve had a significant personal growth year in 2026, it may not be enough to promote him to Triple-A in the spring. A crowded Charlotte Knights infield and an even more overpacked Chicago White Sox infield, especially on the left side of the diamond, will likely keep him with the Barons in March. His age works slightly against him, as he’ll enter the 2027 campaign at age 26 without having seen any Triple-A pitching. However, this hasn’t stopped late-blooming players from becoming significant role players. Even if Briley doesn’t sustain this level of power in 2027, he should still earn a starting job on the Knights (or another Triple-A club) by the middle of the season.

item.description: Will McDonald IV #9, Jowon Briggs #91 and Minkah Fitzpatrick #29 of the New York Jets celebrate after a stop against the Los Angeles Chargers. Don’t bank on the tank. That was the message the Jets delivered to their fans with Sunday’s 27-24 victory over the Chargers . A segment of Jets fans now view wins as losses because it damages the team’s draft position, but Jets players and coaches are trying to win games, not worry about next April’s draft. The Jets now are 3-8 with six games remaining. Some of those games look winnable, so the pro-tank crowd now is bracing itself for more sad Sunday nights watching their draft positioning sink. It starts this week against a Dolphins team that is starting Kyle McCord at quarterback. The Jets play the Cardinals on Dec. 20, when Arizona could be starting rookie Carson Beck or 40-year-old journeyman Josh Johnson under center. The next week, they face a suddenly vulnerable Patriots team that may have ex-Giants backup Tommy DeVito as its starter. The Jets finish the season in Buffalo; the Bills, who are currently 9-1, may have their playoff position wrapped up by then and could play backups. All of this has Jets fans worried about a potential 6-11 or 7-10 finish that could send their draft pick outside of the top 10. The Jets have three first-round picks in 2027, so even if the Jets win some games down the stretch, they could end up with a high pick. Indianapolis traded the Jets its first-round pick last year in the package for Sauce Gardner , and the Colts’ pick looks destined to be in the top five. At the time, the Colts seemed playoff-bound, but they have bottomed out and now are playing out the string. item.title: The full analysis of Chivas' commanding win over Cruz Azul
item.description: The full analysis of Chivas' commanding win over Cruz Azul Guadalajara capped off the Apertura 2026 regular season with a statement win. The 1-0 victory over Cruz Azul on Matchday 17 showcased the competitiveness, solidity and tactical versatility that have defined Gabriel Milito’s team, who made home advantage count to secure top spot and head into the playoffs full of confidence. The keys to the Red and Whites’ victory: Intensity and penetration from the start: Chivas set a high tempo from the opening minutes, pressed high and constantly looked to get in behind the Cruz Azul defense. Santiago Sandoval was central to that approach, moving across the front line, while Bryan González’s runs in behind, Richard Ledezma’s forward surges and Daniel Aguirre’s overlapping runs provided different ways to threaten. Solidity to control the game: The Rebaño once again showed why they have the best defense in the tournament. Diego Campillo delivered another top-class performance, winning his duels with Gabriel Fernández and limiting the Cruz Azul striker’s opportunities. Beyond his defensive assurance, he also contributed on the ball, including a pass that nearly led to a goal for Santiago Sandoval. Sandoval, a headache for the Cruz Azul defense: The young Chivas player stood out for his link-up play, movement and ability to receive on the turn under pressure. His first touches allowed him to beat opponents, win duels and consistently draw fouls: he was fouled six times during the match, a reflection of how difficult he was to contain. Efraín Álvarez, the star of the night: In addition to scoring the winner, the midfielder once again demonstrated his importance to the team’s overall play. He excelled in combination play, linked up with Ledezma through switches of play and nearly added an assist after a superb individual move ended with a through ball for Bryan González. His attacking impact in the closing stretch of the regular season has been significant: he was directly involved in three goals over the last three Liga MX matches, with a goal and an assist against Atlante and another goal against Cruz Azul. A meaningful victory heading into the playoffs The win carried extra significance because it came against an opponent in excellent form. Guadalajara beat Cruz Azul for the first time in ten matches and ended La Máquina’s seven-match unbeaten run, which included five wins and two draws. Chivas not only made home advantage count but also confirmed their ability to compete in every phase of the game, combining attacking quality with the defensive solidity that saw them concede the fewest goals in the Apertura 2026. Guadalajara made a statement on the final matchday and will enter the playoffs as the top seed, with a team performance that offered plenty of encouraging signs. item.title: Fury reveals schizophrenia diagnosis ahead of Joshua clash
item.description: Tyson Fury will face British heavyweight rival Anthony Joshua in Cardiff next month (Chanakarn LAOSARAKHAM) Tyson Fury has said he was diagnosed with schizophrenia soon after his world title win over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015. "Words can't explain the darkness I was in," said the heavyweight boxer. "It was like a living version of the pits of hell. "I thought I would end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much. "The anxiety was crippling me. I just could not overcome it and that's when I went and saw the psychiatrist down in London." Fury has made the revelations about his mental health in a documentary which will be released by Netflix on Friday. The 38-year-old is preparing for the long-awaited all-British heavyweight fight against Anthony Joshua, a fellow former world champion, in Cardiff on December 11 -- a bout that will be broadcast live on Netflix. Fury recalled hearing the radio talking to him, and begging wife Paris to get him out of the hospital because "the Illuminati" wanted him. Following his victory over Klitschko, Fury gained weight and struggled with alcohol and drug addiction. "It got that bad I was hearing voices in my mind," he said. "I wouldn't be able to sit and have a conversation because I'd be hearing stuff in my mind. "I didn't know where to turn and no-one knew what to do. I really needed help, or check into rehab or something. I never got a break from it for years. I wanted to be what I thought was normal again." After Fury was released from hospital, a diagnosis of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder was confirmed. Fury said a turning point in his life came when he was on a night out for Halloween in 2017. "I looked around and could see all the young people and I thought, 'I had the world in my hands and I threw it all away, and now I'm a fat mess addicted to alcohol'," he said. But Fury added he channelled his disgust into a comeback which led him to return to training, focus more on his family and claim another world title when he beat Deontay Wilder in 2020. jdg/nf

item.title: USA joint bid and UK confirmed as 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cup hosts
item.description: FIFA announced Monday that the USA will co-host the 2031 Women's World Cup with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, while the UK will host in 2035 (OZAN KOSE) FIFA on Monday confirmed that a joint bid led by the United States will host the expanded, 48-team Women's World Cup in 2031, while the United Kingdom will host the following edition in 2035. The winning bids were waved through by acclamation after FIFA president Gianni Infantino confirmed the USA in partnership with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica was the "sole candidacy" to host in 2031, when the tournament will feature 48 teams for the first time. The joint English, Scottish, Northern Irish and Welsh bid was also the only candidacy for 2035. Infantino had already revealed last year that the respective bids for 2031 and 2035 were unchallenged and therefore set to be awarded the tournaments, with both being officially rubber-stamped at a virtual gathering of FIFA's member associations. "As of 2031 there will be 48 teams and four hosts," said Infantino. "This is an incredible growth in just a few years." The next Women's World Cup will take place next year in Brazil, running from June 24 to July 25. It will feature 32 teams, with the final at the Maracana Stadium in Rio de Janeiro. Spain go into that tournament as the holders after winning the last Women's World Cup held in Australia and New Zealand in 2023, when they defeated current European champions England in the final. The US co-hosted this year's men's World Cup, with the majority of matches being played on American soil, including the final at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey which was won by Spain. That was the first men's edition featuring 48 teams. The USA has hosted the Women's World Cup twice before, in 1999 and 2003, and is also the most successful nation in the tournament's history, having lifted the trophy four times. - 'Landmark moment' - US Soccer reacted to the announcement by saying the awarding of the 2031 tournament gave the country the chance to "build on the momentum" of this year's World Cup as well as the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The United States are the reigning Olympic women's football champions. No senior men's or women's World Cup has been played in the UK since England hosted and won the men's edition in 1966. A joint statement by the four UK national associations described the announcement as "a landmark moment". It is not yet known which cities will host matches at the respective tournaments, but most matches in 2031 are likely to take place in the United States while England can expect to have the lion's share of venues in 2035. The UK bid proposed 22 stadiums in total, with 16 in England, three in Wales, two in Scotland and one in Northern Ireland. Scottish Football Association chief executive Ian Maxwell said the two venues in the country would be the 52,000-seat Hampden Park in Glasgow as well as Hibernian's 20,000-seat Easter Road home in Edinburgh. item.description: 📹 In a dull affair, São Paulo lead, but Botafogo snatch a draw Botafogo and São Paulo drew 1-1 at the Estádio Nilton Santos on Monday (23) in Matchday 36 of the 2026 Brasileirão. The match was typical of two teams that have disappointed their fans throughout the season and have little left to play for in the closing stages of the league campaign. São Paulo opened the scoring in the first half through Pedro Lima, who finished off an assist from Luciano. Botafogo, meanwhile, showed little ability to put their opponents under pressure. The equalizer finally came late in the match, with Tiquinho Soares pouncing on a rebound off the goalkeeper. item.title: Huskies start fast, can’t hold on in Maui Invitational loss to BYU
item.description: LAHAINIA, HI- NOVEMBER 23: Tayshawn Comer #12 of the Washington Huskies goes to the basket over Nate Pickens #2 of the BYU Cougars in the first half during a first round Southwest Maui Invitational college basketball game at the Lahaina Civic Center on November 23, 2026 in Lahaina, Hawaii. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Though its coaching staff would likely roll their eyes at the mention of it, a moral victory was achieved in Washington’s 83-77 loss to #19 BYU in the opening round of the Maui Invitational. Given the trajectory of the two programs, a blowout loss suffered by the Huskies wouldn’t have been a surprise. For most, it was the expectation. Instead, UW looked the best it has under third year head coach Danny Sprinkle. Washington flew to Hawaii with an unbeaten record to its name. Victories over Colgate, Mississippi Valley State, Simon Fraser and Utah Tech are not enough to gloat, but victories are victories nonetheless. To go from those four opponents, to facing a nationally ranked foe is a significant leap, yet the Dawgs handled it well. Washington built a double digit lead within the first 10 minutes of the game. The hot start was especially impressive given UW wasn’t knocking down a bevy of three pointers. The Huskies were simply outplaying the Cougars and forced them out of their comfort zone. Eventually BYU returned the favor. Momentum shifted significantly in the second half when BYU’s full court press disrupted UW’s offensive flow. As UW’s scoring slowed, BYU’s opened up. After a first half that saw Washington outscore BYU 39-31, the Cougars outscored the Huskies 52-38 the rest of the way. Washington received its biggest scoring contributions from LeJuan Watts, who had 21 points off the bench and Ryan Beasley, who added 20. Lathan Sommerville was busy in the paint and added 13 points along with nine rebounds. Washington is back in action tomorrow against Clemson. The Tigers lost 82-62 to Ole Miss prior to UW’s clash with BYU.

item.description: ‘You Can’t Have a Game Like This’ — Former NFL LB ‘Concerned’ About Trevor Lawrence After Jaguars QB’s Struggles vs. Giants Trevor Lawrence had a rough afternoon in the Jacksonville Jaguars’ 23-18 Week 11 loss to the New York Giants, and it brought back memories of the quarterback fans thought they had moved on from. Lawrence completed 25 of 47 passes for 301 yards, one touchdown and two costly interceptions, ending the Jaguars’ three-game winning streak. Routine throws went missing, and Jacksonville managed just one touchdown on six trips inside the red zone. Former NFL linebacker Emmanuel Acho saw the same thing. He said this version of Lawrence reminded him of the old one, and that is a concern even with the Jaguars sitting at 7-3. Emmanuel Acho Worried by Trevor Lawrence’s Week 11 Struggles Speaking on the “Speakeasy” podcast Monday, Acho said every quarterback is allowed a bad game, but it was the way Lawrence threw his interceptions that bothered him. In Acho’s view, a team with real Super Bowl hopes can’t afford to give the ball away like that. “This game just worried me because it was flashbacks of old Trevor,” Acho said . “Everybody’s afforded a bad game. But in order to get where the Jags want to go, ’cause it’s fair to have Super Bowl expectations and conversations, Trevor, you can’t have a game like this. It would be one thing if Trevor’s interceptions were, like, tipped-ball interceptions or through-the-receiver’s-hands interceptions.” The former linebacker said the picks weren’t flukes, and he worried about what could happen if they showed up in the playoffs. item.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Sung-Mun Song #24 of the San Diego Padres leads off second base during the third inning against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Petco Park on September 27, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). Sung-Mun Song When Song played in Korea, he was an absolute star. In MLB, not so much. In his final season in the KBO, Song slashed .315/.387/.530 with 26 home runs. It was an incredible year. Because of that production, the Padres decided to sign him to a four-year, $15 million deal. At the time, Song was one of the most coveted international free agents. He’s yet to make good on that pedigree. Overall Grade: D Spring Training went well enough. Song posted a .235/.381/.412 slash line in eight Cactus League games. However, his spring was cut short when he suffered an oblique strain that kept him off of the Opening Day roster. He worked his way back from the injury and began the season in Triple-A. He was solid there (.655 OPS), and cracked the big-league roster in late April. Song struggled to acclimate to the big leagues in his first year. He was relegated to a bench player, though the infielder’s bat struggled even in those limited instances. The infielder hit .191/.291/.244 in 78 games (131 at-bats) with the Padres. He did hit one home run, notching the first of his career against the Chicago Cubs in Wrigley Field. It didn’t make headlines because the Padres went on to lose that game by a ridiculous 20 runs. There were flashes of potential. Song went 2-for-4 with a double versus the San Francisco Giants in his second MLB game. He went 2-for-2 with a walk and a stolen base against the New York Mets later in the season, and went 3-for-3 against the Kansas City Royals. But that was it. Song did manage to bat .273 with runners in scoring position. If he can continue that trend while boosting the rest of his offense, he could become a valuable part of the roster in 2027.

Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier.
